name: COUNTIF
description: COUNTIF counts the number of cells in a range that meet a specified condition. It's the counting counterpart of SUMIF — instead of summing matching values, it counts how many matches exist.
tldr: COUNTIF counts cells that match a condition. Give it a range and a criterion (like '>100' or 'East') and it tells you how many cells pass the test.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: The range of cells to count. Each cell is evaluated against the criteria.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: The condition that determines which cells to count. Can be a number, text, comparison, or wildcard pattern.

basicExample.description: Count how many students scored 80 or above
basicExample.explanation: The formula checks each cell in A2:A30 and counts how many contain a value of 80 or higher.

advancedExamples.title: Count occurrences of specific text
advancedExamples.explanation: Exact text match (case-insensitive). Counts all cells containing exactly 'Yes' (or 'yes', 'YES').

advancedExamples.title: Count with wildcard for partial text
advancedExamples.description: Count cells containing 'error' anywhere in the text
advancedExamples.explanation: The asterisks match any surrounding text. '*error*' catches 'Error found', 'Type error', 'Syntax error message'.

advancedExamples.title: Count non-blank cells
advancedExamples.description: Count how many cells in a range are not empty
advancedExamples.explanation: "<>" (not equal to empty) counts all cells that have any content — numbers, text, or formulas.

howItWorks: COUNTIF scans each cell in the range and checks it against your criteria. For exact text matches, it does a case-insensitive comparison. For numeric criteria like '>100', it evaluates the comparison operator. For wildcards, * matches any sequence of characters and ? matches exactly one character. Each cell that passes the test increments the count by 1. The result is a single number: the total count of matching cells.

howToSteps.name: Select the range
howToSteps.text: Choose the cells you want to count through (e.g., A2:A50).

howToSteps.name: Define the criteria
howToSteps.text: Specify what to count: a number (5), text ('Yes'), comparison ('>=80'), or wildcard ('*error*').

limitations: COUNTIF handles only one condition. For multiple conditions, use COUNTIFS.
Text criteria are case-insensitive — 'yes' and 'YES' both match.
COUNTIF cannot count cells by color, font, or other visual formatting.
For counting unique values, COUNTIF alone isn't sufficient — combine with UNIQUE or advanced formulas.

commonErrors.cause: The criteria text/number doesn't exist in the range, or there's a formatting mismatch
commonErrors.fix: Double-check that the values in the range actually match your criteria. Watch for trailing spaces.

commonErrors.cause: Numbers stored as text won't match numeric criteria like '>100'
commonErrors.fix: Convert text numbers to actual numbers, or use text criteria: =COUNTIF(A2:A50, ">100") may not work on text-formatted numbers.

commonErrors.cause: Wildcard criteria treating numbers as text
commonErrors.fix: Wildcards only work on text content. Numeric cells won't match wildcard patterns.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: COUNTIF works identically in Google Sheets with the same syntax.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Google Sheets COUNTIFS also works for multiple conditions, same as Excel.

faq.question: What's the difference between COUNTIF and COUNTIFS?
faq.answer: COUNTIF uses one condition. COUNTIFS uses multiple conditions: =COUNTIFS(A2:A50, "East", B2:B50, ">100") counts rows where both A is 'East' AND B is >100.

faq.question: Can COUNTIF count blank cells?
faq.answer: Yes. Use =COUNTIF(A2:A50, "") to count empty cells, or =COUNTIF(A2:A50, "<>") to count non-empty cells.

faq.question: How do I count unique values?
faq.answer: In Excel 365, use =COUNTA(UNIQUE(A2:A50)). In older Excel, use =SUMPRODUCT(1/COUNTIF(A2:A50, A2:A50)) for unique counts.

faq.question: Can COUNTIF count by cell color?
faq.answer: No. COUNTIF cannot filter by background or font color. You need VBA or manual filtering for color-based counting.
